correctness.rationale: The ten-triple-point Desargues incidence forces thirty exceptional incidence nodes and fifteen ordinary double nodes; local blow-up produces a 20-component, 45-node stable curve of genus 26. A Petersen block-identity proves the nonzero eigenvalue product and exact determinant. Modular local Smith reductions in the standalone Python program, independently for two deleted-vertex orbits at four primes, produce the stated invariant factors with product equal to this determinant. All hypotheses for the cited semistable Néron identification are explicit.

value.rationale: This is a naturally defined, complete geometric degeneration invariant for the classical Desargues ten-line arrangement. Its invariant factors determine 2-, 3-, 5- and 7-primary component structures and Néron component group for thickness-one models, going beyond the graph spectrum/spanning-tree count. The operation of resolving the ten actual triple points is canonical; no artificial subgraph or arbitrary numerical slice is imposed.
